managed_allocations.proof: Static source review: Burst jobs accept NativeArray fields only; no List, LINQ, Instantiate, or GlobalRegistry polling in Shinobu socket jobs. PlayerBuilder caches DataVault and ConstructionManager before active snap calls, stores ModuleTemplate preview pose/scale as data instead of activeBuildable.ghostPrefab pool spawn or runtime proxy acquisition, and no longer owns a managed List<MonoBehaviour> placement-rule scan buffer or active IBuildPlacementRule interface dispatch lane. The active SHINOBU snap update now reads existing Vault socket/module counters and computes its topology hash from Vault module and connection-pair rows; it no longer pulls ConstructionManager.SpawnedModules, GameObject identity, ModuleMarker components, or transforms to hydrate target socket rows. Construction occupied-cell validation now reads ConstructionSocketModuleDTO.RootAup rows from Vault and no longer hydrates ConstructionBuilderOccupancy from managed scene modules. HectonBlueprintPreviewBatch now binds Vault handles only through EnsureBuffersCold() in Awake/OnEnable; active preview upload reads cached buffers and fails closed. SHINOBU snap occupancy no longer scans or marks ModuleSocket authoring components; placement commits write SocketStateDTO.ConnectionStatus and SocketConnectionPairDTO rows directly in Vault from the placement command pose, not placedModule.transform. Black-box dump APIs no longer allocate dump-sized byte[] mirrors; they stream NativeArray bytes through ReadOnlySpan<byte> over the unsafe pointer.

aup_precision.proof: EvaluateSocketSnappingJob uses double3 target-minus-ghost AUP deltas and writes an aligned float4x4; PlayerBuilder writes the snapped root AUP back into GhostPreviewDTO for instant truth plus Dear Lie shader presentation. Construction validation root authority reads ConstructionSocketModuleDTO.RootAup from the SHINOBU Vault module lane through TryUpdateConstructionRootAupFromSocketVault before using the current preview position fallback; the scene-scanning ResolveConstructionRootAup helper was removed. Socket topology hash no longer samples runtime transforms or GameObject identity; it uses Vault counters, ConstructionSocketModuleDTO rows, and SocketConnectionPairDTO rows while AUP rows remain the placement authority. Snapped placement occupancy commit converts the already selected placement command pose to AUP rather than reading the spawned module transform.

csr.proof: Target sockets are bucketed into six direction ranges after excluding Connected, CollisionBlocked, non-finite rows, and invalid direction masks. PackAllowedConnectionBitmask emits no direction bit for invalid authored input; ExtractDirection returns byte.MaxValue for zero or multi-bit masks; AreCompatible rejects invalid masks. Ghost rows preserve source SocketDefinitions indices, use inverse-direction CSR rows at 6 + ghostIndex, and resolve targets through SocketCsrTargetIndices. Invalid ghost rows are flagged NonFinite|CollisionBlocked with zero CSR range. Missing CSR range/index lanes set CapacityExceeded instead of falling back to 0..TargetCount or direct csrIndex rows. Invalid CSR target rows consume budget, mark NonFinite, and continue within the bounded scan. The final snap-result sink rejects invalid target and ghost directions before rotation/pose mutation, so no unknown direction falls back to North.

occupancy.proof: Active snap reads target SocketStateDTO rows already present in Vault and prepares only the owner-local CSR/hash cache from Vault counters and module rows. Construction grid-cell rejection scans finite ConstructionSocketModuleDTO.RootAup rows from the same Vault view and compares AUP-local integer GridPos against the candidate request; ConstructionBuilderOccupancy is not populated from scene modules in PlayerBuilder. Active SHINOBU placement appends the placed module socket rows, marks the target socket and consumed ghost socket Connected, writes one SocketConnectionPairDTO into ConstructionSocketConnections, updates Counters[4], and invalidates cached topology if the commit fails closed. No ModuleSocket component branch remains in SHINOBU occupancy. Burst evaluator rejects Connected rows before scoring. Compatibility remains one unmanaged predicate through AreCompatibilityHashesCompatible(); HashCompatibility reserves 0 for wildcard by remapping non-empty folded zero to 1 before DTO packing.

scalability.proof: Candidate budget and search radius use smooth GlobalQualityWeight curves through SmoothQuality plus math.lerp: 16 to 256 inspected CSR target rows per ghost, no low/high binary switch. EvaluateSocketSnappingJob clamps inspected rows to ResolveCandidateBudget() and uses ResolveSearchRadius() for radius-squared rejection instead of max budget/ultra radius. Budget is consumed when a valid target row is read, before radius/compatibility/alignment rejection, so far bases cannot scan an entire inverse-direction bucket at low quality. Direction CSR removes incompatible and invalid-direction buckets before those quality budgets are consumed. Builder placement validation no longer uses quality to reduce SDF corner truth: CPU hydration and Burst validation always evaluate all eight deterministic bounds corners. Terrain placement truth also uses fixed TerrainProbeTruthCount=9 for both PlayerBuilder and ModularBaseConstructionValidator. GlobalQualityWeight still scales visual shader/material cost, snap search radius, candidate budget, and optional presentation density only. SnapResults reserves 64 ghost rows plus one best-result sink row. Pending and cached poses require scene hash plus query hash over ghost root/yaw/blueprint/socket layout before reuse; the blueprint component uses ResolveShinobuModuleHash with TemplateHashId fallback. Cached Dear Lie pose state is invalidated on query mismatch and failed reducer results, so the shader fake cannot bridge across stale solver truth.

rollback.proof: All Shinobu socket jobs, construction validator placement/connectivity jobs, and HabitatConstructionManager.IntegrityValidationJob use Burst FloatMode.Deterministic and explicit-layout DTO arrays.

visual_fake.proof: DearLieHologram shader and the active BlueprintWireInstanced preview shader use scalar dampening and vertex sine wiggle with guarded normal normalization; PlayerBuilder writes DearLieDampen, GlobalQualityWeight, and DearLieWiggleSpeed through ConstructionPreviewSignal padding at offsets 96/100/104, and HectonBlueprintPreviewBatch applies a quality-scaled decaying material envelope. The preview batch derives BuilderGhostVisualDTO alpha, telemetry SDF sign, and _lastPreviewAllowed from current written validation flags rather than previous-frame _lastPreviewAllowed or pre-sanitized signal flags, requires all scale axes positive before preserving valid flags, and resets the Dear Lie envelope when active preview count reaches zero so the same result/module hash can pulse again after preview re-entry. ModuleTemplate buildables use data-only builder preview pose/scale fields and Vault GhostPreviewDTO rather than active ghostPrefab pool spawn or runtime proxy shell acquisition. Cold fallback proxy materials initialize _H8SnapDampen to 0 so the fake is event-driven. Connected/corridor/hatch state is flags in SocketStateDTO.ConnectionStatus, not instantiated door prefabs. GhostPreviewDTO DearLieActive is fed only from a current-query cached snap pose; stale pose state is cleared before new query truth is presented.

telemetry.proof: Active PlayerBuilder Vault snap path writes ConstructionSocketTelemetryEntry every solver call and dumps Dump_SHINOBU_217.bin on non-finite state. Builder holography writes HolographyTelemetryEntry and dumps Dump_SHINOBU_217_Holography.bin on non-finite/fault state. ModularBaseConstructionValidator writes ConstructionTelemetryEntry and dumps Dump_SHINOBU_217_ConstructionValidation.bin on non-finite validation state. Dump APIs write ReadOnlySpan<byte> over NativeArray pointers to FileStream instead of allocating managed mirror byte arrays. ConstructionPreviewSignal.ModuleHash, construction validation payloads, acoustic source fallback, and FloraExclusionSignal.ModuleHash use the same ResolveShinobuModuleHash fallback as GhostPreviewDTO and the Burst job.

frame_authority.proof: PlayerBuilder and HectonBlueprintPreviewBatch no longer call Unity Time.frameCount, Time.unscaledTime, or Time.time in the SHINOBU-owned preview/validation/holography path. CaptureShinobuFrameId() and CapturePreviewFrameId() read TimeSliceScheduler.CurrentFrameId and use an owner-local monotonic fallback only if the dispatcher has not published a frame. Dear Lie animation phase is frame-derived as frame/120, avoiding wall-clock drift in BuilderGhostStateDTO.ValidationStateHash.

runtime_origin_signal_bridge_removal.proof: PlayerBuilder, HectonBlueprintPreviewBatch, and HabitatConstructionManager no longer call GlobalSignals.CurrentRuntimeOriginAup for SHINOBU snap, holography, or habitat socket AUP conversion. Local finite-guarded helpers read HectonFloatingOrigin.CurrentTotalOffsetDouble as double3, pass that origin into jobs, add it before authored socket AUP hydration, and subtract it in double precision before runtime Vector3 casts.

semantic_rules.proof: IBuildPlacementRule.cs was deleted. PlayerBuilder caches semantic rule identity as a byte tag and dispatches to sealed DeepDrillModule.ValidatePlacementWithService() or AutonomousExtractorModule.ValidatePlacementWithRuntime(). The drill route consumes cached IInteractionSignalService with runtime-position raycast input and no InteractionPacket or Unity Time stamp; CacheActivePlacementRule has no GlobalRegistry.InteractionSignals fallback. The extractor route consumes cached AutonomousExtractorSystem or fails closed, and candidate scoring requires persistent AUP instead of transform-position fallback. Remaining Physics.OverlapSphereNonAlloc is extractor-domain spatial discovery until a resource-node owner publishes an unmanaged snapshot.

mock_grid_counter_scrub.proof: GenerateMockBaseConstructionGrid clears every ConstructionSocketCounters lane before writing module count, socket count, topology version, and flags. Counters[4] connection-pair count is therefore zero for fallback mock grids instead of stale UninitializedMemory data.

cold_counter_lane_seed_guard.proof: InitializeVault checks the existing ConstructionSocketCounters generation handle before requesting it. Absent, too-short, or out-of-capacity lanes are cleared once after handle resolution; valid existing counters are preserved. TryResolveVaultViews remains resolve-only and does not mutate active state.

builder_validation.proof: BuildBuilderGhostStateJob chains into ValidateBuilderGhostPlacementJob; the validate job writes final BuilderGhostStateDTO flags and mirrors those flags plus alpha into the sibling BuilderGhostVisualDTO row before PlayerBuilder consumes output after DispatcherJobFence.TryFinalizeCompleted. CPU SDF hydration and Burst validation share ResolveBuilderGhostCornerIndex and always evaluate BuilderGhostSdfCornerCount, exactly eight bounds corners, so telemetry records a constant all-eight placement proof. HectonBlueprintPreviewBatch telemetry also writes BuilderGhostSdfCornerCount directly and no longer calls the removed sample-count helper. Pending validation results are guarded by the active buildable generation plus a query hash over module hash, preview pose, rotation, proxy bounds center/size, and snap/DearLie flags. Active validation uses the cached TryResolveShinobuSocketVault gate rather than GlobalRegistry.DataVault; DispatcherJobFence.TryComplete is confined to teardown helpers.

builder_holography_generation_handles.proof: HectonBlueprintPreviewBatch stores VaultGenerationHandle descriptors for builder ghost state, visual, telemetry, and indirect-args lanes. EnsureBuffersCold acquires them through GetGenerationHandle; active TryReadCachedBuffers resolves phase-local NativeArray views through IDataVault.TryResolveHandle with no VaultBufferHandle, ResolveBuffer, GetBufferHandle, or .Resolve(vault) residue in the batch.

active_selection.proof: CycleBuildable and DebugDeployActiveBuildable do not call BindRuntimeReferences. SetActiveBuildable does not force-complete pending snap or builder-ghost jobs; active selection and post-placement preview refresh use DespawnGhost(forceValidationReset:false). Socket snap and builder ghost validation jobs store active buildable generation at schedule time, and stale naturally completed results are discarded before cached pose/result use.

build_cost_buffer_fence.proof: HabitatConstructionManager build-cost checks use fixed cold scratch buffers: PlayerInventory.ItemPlacement[1024] plus cost hash/remaining/removed/item buffers sized to 32 rows. Active resource checks fail closed on oversized inventories or authored cost rows instead of growing managed arrays or truncating resource evidence.

integrity_graph_cache_signature.proof: HabitatConstructionManager computes its existing graph cache signature from SHINOBU socket Vault topology when Vault module count matches the construction registry count. The signature folds module/socket/connection counters, ConstructionSocketModuleDTO AUP/rotation/socket/topology fields, and SocketConnectionPairDTO connection rows. The absent/count-mismatched Vault fallback hashes ModuleHashId, family, AUP-quantized root, and rotation bits instead of Unity GetInstanceID. This is partial cache-key closure only: full Vault-only integrity graph source remains blocked until support-root/family and resource-mass facts are published in an unmanaged construction-owner route.

integrity_adjacency_corruption_fence.proof: HabitatConstructionManager validates connection endpoints before adjacency degree counting and final adjacency writes, checks AdjacencyRanges capacity before mutation, fences connection count against _connectionCapacity, rejects adjacency-count overflow, and invalidates the existing graph cache on malformed rows. AddConnection rejects negative endpoints and self-loops before writing the connection row.

tuner_read_purity.proof: ModularBaseConstructionValidator.TryReadTunerSettingsFromVault returns default on failure and only writes settings after a successful finite Vault read. PlayerBuilder explicitly falls back to GetTunerSettings when that read fails, so fallback provenance is not hidden inside a TryRead facade.

validator_generation_descriptors.proof: ModularBaseConstructionValidator stores VaultGenerationHandle descriptors for tuning, telemetry, bounds, and occupancy lanes. Explicit ensure/write routes use GetGenerationHandle and read routes use IDataVault.TryResolveHandle. Focused source scan shows no VaultBufferHandle, GetBufferHandle, ResolveBuffer, .Resolve(vault), or TryGetBuffer residue.

surface_hit_ownership.proof: PlayerBuilder.TryGetBuildHit does not call Physics.RaycastNonAlloc and no longer owns a RaycastHit buffer. It consumes cached IInteractionSignalService.TryRaycastPrimary with finite runtime origin/direction/range guards and a stable builder requester id; missing interaction service fails closed.

builder_deconstruction_target_registry.proof: PlayerBuilder resolves deconstruction hit colliders through LaserCutterTargetRegistry.TryResolveModule instead of GetComponentInParent<BaseModule> after the interaction-owned raycast. BaseModule.OnEnable populates the fixed collider registry; missing rows fail closed with no scene hierarchy fallback.

extractor_runtime_registry.proof: AutonomousExtractorSystem no longer owns a growable List module registry. It uses fixed AutonomousExtractorModule[256] plus _moduleCount, bounded registration, and explicit compaction without List.Add/RemoveAt. DeepDrillModule no longer owns a static growable List active-provider registry; it uses fixed DeepDrillModule[128] plus s_ActiveModuleCount and swap-with-tail removal. AdvanceExtractionJob uses explicit 32-byte input/result rows, FloatMode.Deterministic, CompileSynchronously=true, FloatPrecision.Standard, and NoAlias input/result NativeArrays. The unreferenced AutonomousExtractorJobs.cs duplicate was deleted. Resource-host semantic migration remains blocked until Hecton8.World.Contracts exposes extractor-capable host snapshots; direct Hecton8.World.Economy dependency was rejected.

h_phi_vault_status.lifecycle: BindRuntimeReferences cold-calls InitializeVault to request socket descriptors; TryResolveVaultViews now only resolves phase-local NativeArray views and does not allocate/grow buffers. HectonBlueprintPreviewBatch binds builder-holography VaultBufferHandle descriptors in EnsureBuffersCold() during Awake/OnEnable; active preview ticks read cached buffers only. Active SHINOBU snap and grid occupancy consume pre-published Vault module/socket rows and fail closed for snap target absence; occupied-cell checking treats zero module rows as an empty construction source for first placement and records the legacy-module publisher gap as residual risk. PlayerBuilder no longer hydrates target sockets or occupied-cell scratch from ConstructionManager.SpawnedModules. SHINOBU snap placement owns occupancy through Vault rows and connection pairs, not private NativeArray/List state or ModuleSocket scene scans.

residual_risks.risk: dotnet build was launched after CPU averaged 29.96 percent. SHINOBU project-file visibility was fixed; remaining SHINOBU-local compile error is unresolved VaultGenerationHandle<T> because Hecton8.Core.csproj references stale Library/ScriptAssemblies/Hecton8.Core.Memory.dll while source GlobalDataVault.cs defines the newer API.

PlacementGhost and RepairDroneHub still contain adjacent non-socket PhysX queries outside the new socket route. AutonomousExtractorSystem still contains one non-alloc semantic-rule overlap; SHINOBU removed its interface dispatch/runtime allocation/transform fallback and growable registry/Fast-Burst residue but did not invent a resource-node spatial snapshot owner.

Existing Hecton8.World.Contracts exposes ore position/type read lanes through IWorldResourceSpawnerReadModel. It does not expose extractor-support flag, host diameter, yield item hash, depletion state, or stable claim identity. Direct Hecton8.World.Economy references are rejected to preserve the compile wall; world-resource ownership must publish an extractor-capable unmanaged host snapshot before SHINOBU can remove the remaining extractor semantic overlap.

AutonomousExtractorSystem still owns private NativeArray SOA lanes for cycle timers, job inputs/results, buffered counts, and completion counters. This pass fixed deterministic ABI and managed registry growth only. Migrating those lanes to GlobalDataVault needs an extractor-owned BufferID route card and owner approval, because they are runtime extractor state rather than SHINOBU socket adaptor truth.

HabitatConstructionManager can use socket Vault topology as a deterministic cache signature, but the full integrity graph still cannot be sourced exclusively from ConstructionSocketModuleDTO rows because support-root/family and resource-mass facts are not owned by that DTO route. Guessing those values from module hash or bounds was rejected.

ConstructionRuntimeProxyFactory still creates cold fallback GameObjects for legacy proxy shells and placed no-prefab modules; ModuleTemplate active preview no longer uses activeBuildable.ghostPrefab or TryAcquireGhostProxy, and no per-frame socket trigger creation remains.

PlayerBuilder no longer scans ConstructionManager.SpawnedModules for occupied-cell truth. Legacy modules that have not published ConstructionSocketModuleDTO rows will not be visible to the pure Vault occupied-cell check until their owner migrates to the same Vault publisher route.
